## Slide Outline & Speaking Notes

### Slide 1: Title & Overview
- **Title:** Molecular Toxicity Prediction on Tox21: Phase 2 Deep Learning & Hybrid Benchmark
- **Subtitle:** Graph Neural Networks, Multi-Modal Hybrids, and Rigorous Empirical Controls
- **Presenter Notes:** Introduce the team and Phase 2 objective: an out-of-distribution benchmark comparing classical trees against neural message passing and multi-modal hybrids under zero-leakage governance.

### Slide 2: Chemical Context & Representation Limits
- **Title:** 1. Chemical Context: Why Traditional Fingerprints Hit a Ceiling
- **Key Message:** Fixed circular Morgan fingerprints (ECFP4) suffer from bit collisions, rigid unweighted hashing, and inability to capture continuous spatial/conjugated geometry. Graph neural networks address this by treating compounds as natural molecular graphs.

### Slide 3: Tox21 Benchmark & Scaffold Splits
- **Title:** 2. Tox21 Benchmark: Bioassays & Out-of-Distribution Scaffold Shifts
- **Key Message:** 7,709 compounds across 12 bioassays with severe imbalance (~8% toxic hits) and ~20% missing labels. Bemis-Murcko scaffold splitting clusters molecules by cyclic core, enforcing zero scaffold overlap between train (6,167), val (771), and test (771).

### Slide 4: Graph Featurization & Mathematical Invariances
- **Title:** 3. Graph Construction: 39 Continuous Features & Invariances
- **Key Message:** 33 continuous atom node features and 6 bond edge features. Permutation invariance guaranteed by Set2Set attention readout (unit-tested). Masked class-weighted binary cross-entropy loss handles missing labels cleanly.

### Slide 5: Deep Learning Architectures (GCN vs MPNN)
- **Title:** 4. Deep Architectures: GCN vs. Message Passing (MPNN)
- **Key Message:** Contrast isotropic GCN (ignores bond types, ~56k params) with Gilmer et al. MPNN (continuous edge network A(e_vw), GRU node updates, Set2Set pooling, ~628k params).

### Slide 6: Hybrid Model Design (H1 & H2)
- **Title:** 5. Hybrid Design: Fusing Message Passing with Physicochemical Priors
- **Key Message:** 
  - **H1 Multi-Modal Hybrid (`mpnn+desc`):** Concatenates learned Set2Set graph embedding ($R^{128}$) with 213 RDKit descriptors ($R^{128}$) before classification.
  - **H2 Late-Fusion Ensemble (`ens_xgb_mpnn+desc`):** Rank-averages Phase 1 XGBoost and DL H1 with equal 0.5/0.5 weights fixed a priori.

### Slide 7: Protocol & Test-Set Discipline
- **Title:** 6. Protocol & Test-Set Discipline: Zero-Leakage Governance
- **Key Message:** Tuning strictly on scaffold validation split (max 8 configs per family). Configs frozen in `best_configs_dl.json` (commit `0aebd87`) before test set was scored. Test set touched once across 3 random seeds.

### Slide 8: Main Benchmark Results on Scaffold Test Split
- **Title:** 7. Primary Benchmark: Out-of-Distribution Scaffold Results
- **Key Message:** 
  - H1 ($0.3553$ PR AUC) beats FP-MLP control ($0.3429$) on 9/12 endpoints.
  - H2 ensemble ($0.3945$ PR AUC, $0.7643$ ROC AUC) achieves lowest seed variance ($\sigma=0.0011$) and beats H1 on 12/12 endpoints ($p=0.00049$).
  - Classical tree baselines (RF $0.4035$, XGB $0.4010$) remain formidable on $\approx$6,200 compounds.

### Slide 9: Chemical Generalization Gap
- **Title:** 8. Chemical Generalization Gap: Random vs. Scaffold Shifts
- **Key Message:** Large performance penalty under scaffold shift across all models ($\Delta\text{PR} \approx 0.160 - 0.195$). FP-MLP suffers the worst penalty ($\Delta=0.1949$), while graph hybrids demonstrate superior generalization robustness ($\Delta=0.1600$).

### Slide 10: Ablation Suite & Negative Control Verification
- **Title:** 9. Ablation Suite: Decisive Negative Control Proof
- **Key Message:** Shuffling descriptors across compounds collapses PR AUC from $0.3553$ to $0.2547$ ($-0.1006$, a $28.3\%$ drop), proving that hybrid gains are driven by genuine molecular physics rather than model capacity.

### Slide 11: Technical Validation & Statistical Rigor
- **Title:** 10. Technical Validation: Statistical Rigor & Sanity Checks
- **Key Message:** Shuffled-label control collapses to $\approx 0.50$ AUC (zero leakage). Single-batch overfit and permutation invariance pass. Paired Wilcoxon tests and joint bootstrap 95% CIs confirm statistical significance.

### Slide 12: Key Takeaways & Practice Guidelines
- **Title:** 11. Takeaways & Guidelines: Computational Toxicology in Practice
- **Key Message:** Never discard descriptor engineering; hybridizing domain physics with graph learning delivers the most robust screening systems. Always evaluate on scaffold splits to uncover true generalization limits.
